answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 9 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The grove multiplier is published, charged in meadow, and haven lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 1664 identities would post 3929 proofs and burn roughly 43 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
